architectural_decisions.rationale: Flutter was chosen for the development of the mobile application to ensure cross-platform compatibility for Android and iOS devices.
The system follows a client-server architecture where the mobile application (frontend) makes requests to a server (backend) that processes them.

The communication between the front-end and the back-end is carried out through a REST API, using JSON format messages for both requests and responses, which guarantees technological independence between both parts.
The backend follows the Hexagonal Architecture (Ports and Adapters) pattern, which allows separating business logic from the framework and infrastructure technologies.
MySQL is used for data persistence, managed through the Django ORM, to clearly define relationships between entities, ensure data integrity, and facilitate schema evolution.
The frontend follows the principles of Clean Architecture, separating responsibilities into Presentation, Domain, and Data layers to improve maintainability and scalability.
The Bloc/Cubit pattern is used for state management to allow a clear separation between the presentation layer and the application logic, avoiding direct dependencies with the backend.
The Factory Pattern is used to dynamically instantiate artificial intelligence services according to the system configuration.
The Repository Pattern is used to isolate data access and simplify the use of the ORM in use cases.
